newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU's Kinnock says new slot rules due soon.
newsitem.headline: EU's Kinnock says new slot rules due soon.

text.p: The European Commission is due in the "very near future" to propose revisions to EU rules forbidding the trade in airports' landing and take-off slots, European Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock said on Friday.
"The debate on that in the Commission will be taking place in the very near future," Kinnock told a news conference.

"When we know that current legislation is being frustrated and beggared by trade in slots that involves sometimes barter and sometimes financial exchange it's time to act to ensure that those activities are not used to restrain competition," he said.

"My proposal is to safeguard those airlines who in current circumstances are excluded," Kinnock said, without giving details of a plan which has faced repeated delays amid Commission divisions about whether airlines should be allowed to cash in some of their slots at busy airports.
Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert has repeatedly opposed slot sales, saying they would give major airlines huge cash injections at the expense of smaller rivals.

Any eventual change to slot sales rules will come too late for British Airways in its planned alliance with AMR Corp's American Airlines, who face competition authorities' demands for the mandatory release of slots at London's Heathrow.
The Commission has ruled out allowing slot sales as part of any package of measures intended to secure the deal's approval.
